data.name: Akshra
data.gender_notes: Akshra is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Akshara is the Sanskrit word for 'letter' or 'character', representing the divine feminine aspect of the written word and knowledge. It is also the name of the Hindu goddess of writing, the embodiment of wisdom and knowledge. The name Akshra carries the meaning “Goddess of Writing” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Akshra usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of writing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Akshra belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Writing.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Akshra total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

The practice of writing one's name with the first letter being Akshara has been an integral part of Hindu rituals, symbolizing one's spiritual teachings, lineage, and self-identification.
